summary: The 2D screening label is illustrative_2d_only. The scenario is the MemPool-2D baseline from W4387010219: a 4.8 x 4.8 mm die, 64 tiles of 425 x 425 um, 40 W TDP, and a paper-reported steady-state Tmax of 46 C above a 27 C ambient from HotSpot v7.0. The experiment kind is custom_2d_steady, so it is steady-state only and has no transient trace. Studio did not run: simulation status is skipped, simulation_allowed is false, and the input gate failed because a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object, and both the floorplan and power_w are empty. The scientific gate also failed and nothing was independently verified. No Studio temperature exists, so comparison_valid is false and the 46 C value cannot be compared numerically with any Studio output. This is not a replication, exact or approximate. The paper's published 2D observable is the die maximum for the 40 W full workload, but its hotspot location is not stated. No pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace data, source commit, or generated-placement assumption applies here, and no input.flp or input.ptrace was produced. A future comparison would need matching location (die maximum), aggregation, steady regime, and boundary assumptions, namely the flip-chip package with a 0.17 K/W heatsink and 50 K/W PCB path. The paper's own 3D MoL results (55 C memory die, 57 C logic die) belong to a different stack and must not be mixed with this 2D baseline. Only qualitative sensitivity can be discussed: package path, power split and floorplan would all strongly affect Tmax, but their effects cannot be quantified from the available inputs.
limitations: Studio did not run, so there is no Studio result, and comparison_valid is false.
The floorplan and power_w are empty. Block coordinates are deferred to ref [38], which is not in the packet.
Only a 40 W total is published. The Fig. 3 percentages have an ambiguous legend mapping and no published splitting rule, so no per-block watts were derived.
No pinned packet assets were supplied. The HotSpot repository and the two DOIs are linked but not pinned, and they do not prove the inputs exist.

The package model is a full flip-chip stack with TIM, spreader, heatsink, C4 bumps, substrate, solder balls, underfill and PCB. The Studio package and material assumptions are not recorded, so boundary conditions are not shown to match.
The 2D die thickness and conductivity are not tabulated. Table I covers the 3D stack with 3.95 mm dies, so applicability to the 4.8 mm 2D die is assumed rather than stated.
The location of the 46 C hotspot, the HotSpot grid resolution and the config files are not given.
HotSpot assumes uniform power density within each block, so intra-block hotspots are not resolved.
The scenario is steady state only, with no power trace, transient, controller, DTM or optimizer.
The 3D MoL/LoM results (55/57 C) are a different configuration and are excluded from any 2D comparison.
Several evidence items lack valid page or asset locators, and the adversarial and independent reviews are unresolved. The figures are paper text, not digitized or verified.
The die and tile dimensions are printed as mm2 and um2 in the paper and were read as edge lengths.

Package is a full flip-chip stack: TIM 100 um at 7 W/mK, heat spreader 5.92 x 5.92 mm, heatsink 7.9 x 7.9 mm with Rconv 0.17 K/W, C4 bumps, substrate, solder balls, underfill and a PCB with 50 K/W natural convection. A simplified Studio thermal stack may not reproduce this path or the 46 C result.
The 2D floorplan is not in this paper (only referenced to ref [38]). No block coordinates or per-block watts are published. Only the die size, tile size, tile count and the 40 W total are given.

The tile power breakdown (cores, I$, SPM, interconnects, others) appears only as percentages in Fig. 3, and the legend-to-slice mapping is ambiguous. Splitting the 40 W total would need a published rule, so it cannot be treated as paper-derived watts per block.
HotSpot assumes uniform power density within each block, so intra-block hotspots are not resolved.

The paper's main subject is 3D (MoL/LoM) stacking: F2F bonding, a BEOL layer at 1.2 W/mK, a thinned 5 um logic die. None of this applies to the selected 2D baseline, and the 3D results (55/57 C) must not be mixed with it.
The scenario is steady state only. There is no transient or power-trace data, no controller or DTM, no optimizer, and no reliability analysis in the selected scenario.
The 2D die silicon thickness and thermal conductivity, and the 2D-specific layer stack, are not tabulated. Table I lists 3D memory/logic die layers only.
